STEP 1 - Scene: This is a simple snack or breakfast plate with a slice of toast, a whole red apple and a whole Asian pear. The photo is taken at an angle rather than straight overhead.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A white rimmed dinner plate, about 26 cm across. Area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ 530 cm².

STEP 3 - Items:
- Toasted white bread, one slice
- Whole red apple
- Whole Asian pear (yellow-skinned)

No oil, spread or sauce is visible.

STEP 4 - Area:
- Toast: ~12% (about 64 cm², roughly 9 × 8 cm)
- Apple: ~9% (about 7.5 cm diameter, ~44 cm²)
- Pear: ~10% (about 8 cm diameter, ~50 cm²)

Total coverage is about 31% of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume:
- Toast: 64 cm² × 1.5 cm = 96 ml
- Apple: a whole sphere is better estimated directly, ~7.5 cm diameter ≈ 220 ml
- Pear: ~8 cm diameter ≈ 270 ml

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Toast: bread slices are about 0.3–0.4 g/ml, so 96 ml × 0.35 ≈ 34 g
- Apple: a whole fruit is about 0.85 g/ml, so 220 ml ≈ 185 g
- Pear: about 0.85 g/ml, so 270 ml ≈ 230 g

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Toast: 34 g × 290 kcal/100g ≈ 99 kcal
- Apple: 185 g × 52 kcal/100g ≈ 96 kcal
- Pear: 230 g × 42 kcal/100g ≈ 97 kcal

Total ≈ 449 g, ≈ 292 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A medium apple weighs about 180 g and an Asian pear about 200–250 g, so these weights are plausible. A slice of toast at about 30–35 g is typical.
